headline: Highest risk is medium: shared broad egress and overlapping file/API surfaces can leak support data into the travel gateway, while prompt-injection and cascading errors remain plausible but not directly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest customer messages and integrations, while Plano exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and config file surface. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven; however, if Chatwoot content is forwarded into Plano prompts, attacker-controlled text could steer outputs. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not observed.
conditions: IF Chatwoot conversation text is copied or forwarded into Plano prompts
IF Plano is configured to treat upstream text as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed system prompt that strips instruction-like text from Chatwoot content
Require manual review before forwarding customer messages into Plano
Use a delimiter and provenance tag for all imported text
Disable any automation that pipes Chatwoot transcripts into Plano
requires-engineering: add prompt-firewall parsing between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, orders, messages, and reports, and Plano has broad network egress plus an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Even without a shared workspace, any operator who routes Chatwoot content through Plano can expose sensitive support data to a third-party inference backend. The interaction is plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records or messages are sent through Plano
IF Plano forwards prompts to an external model provider
mitigations: Restrict Plano to redacted or synthetic inputs
Disable forwarding of Chatwoot tickets containing personal data
Add a data-loss review step before any API call
Log and sample outbound payloads for sensitive fields
requires-engineering: enforce DLP rules on the Chatwoot-to-Plano path

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot is a customer-support app with API integrations, while Plano is an AI gateway with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and a config file surface. Neither profile shows shared writable filesystem access, git mutation, or multiple-instance contention, so direct write conflict is not evidenced. The only overlap is network/API use, which is a limited conflict surface.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external API quota or shared mutable backend
IF an operator maps both to the same config or secret store
mitigations: Separate credentials for each agent
Use distinct API quotas or projects
Avoid shared writable directories
Check for duplicate config paths before deployment
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable backend

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, and Plano exposes an LLM gateway that may treat upstream text as model input. If Chatwoot output is fed into Plano without verification, Plano can amplify hallucinations or malformed instructions into downstream actions or responses. No verification step is documented, so the unsafe path is plausible in default integrations.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are used as authoritative input to Plano
IF Plano responses are acted on without human or rule-based verification
mitigations: Insert a verification step before any downstream action
Require citations or source links for generated claims
Limit Plano to drafting, not execution
Review a sample of chained outputs daily
requires-engineering: add schema validation between Chatwoot and Plano

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and related records, while Plano touches logs, traces, and metrics and has broad network egress. The profiles do not state residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch cannot be ruled out; uncertainty escalates to medium because sensitive customer data could flow into a logging-heavy gateway. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is routed through Plano logs or traces
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls not enforced by either agent
mitigations: Mask personal data before it reaches Plano
Set short log retention on Plano
Review residency requirements before enabling the integration
Disable verbose tracing for customer payloads
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention and residency controls
